disposition_reason: Primary flame AAS data for arsenic, copper, iron, mercury, lead and zinc in seven laboratory-processed cereal and root and tuber flours (Tables 1 to 3).

study.design: Laboratory processing of market-bought raw crops into flour and analysis of trace metals and aflatoxins
study.method: Dry ashing at 550 °C, HNO3 dissolution, flame AAS (Buck Scientific 210VGP), including As and Hg by flame AAS
study.lod_text: not reported for metals (aflatoxin LOD/LOQ only)
study.qa: Spike recoveries 93-97% for As, Cu, Fe, Hg, Pb and Zn; no CRM

unresolved: Collection or purchase dates are not reported.
Text says the maximum Cu in root and tuber flour was 3.67 mg/kg, but Table 1 prints cocoyam flour Cu 6.63 ± 0.02 mg/kg; table used.
Text says As and Pb were 'detected in all the root and tuber and cereal flour' samples, while the tables print As < 0.01 for all flours and Pb < 0.01 for five of seven.
Arsenic and mercury by flame AAS with a 0.01 mg/kg threshold is analytically doubtful; non-detects are weak evidence.
n = duplicate samples per flour (Data analysis section); number of independent lots not stated.
Table 3 repeats Tables 1 and 2 with different superscripts; not extracted twice.
